characters.name: Adam Young

characters.description: A young woman who is a practicing witch and occultist, and the last descendant of a seventeenth-century prophetess. She has spent her life guided by an inherited book of eerily accurate predictions, and she comes to Lower Tadfield on its instructions, trying to work out how to head off the disaster the prophecies foretell.
characters.name: Anathema Device

characters.description: A mild, awkward young man and hopeless amateur with computers and machines, which tend to break in his presence. Looking for something more meaningful, he answers an odd recruiting notice and becomes a modern member of a nearly defunct witch-hunting order, a role that sends him toward Lower Tadfield.
characters.name: Newton Pulsifer

characters.description: The cantankerous, unwashed, and deeply paranoid leader of the Witchfinder Army, a centuries-old witch-hunting organization now reduced to almost nothing but himself. Gruff and suspicious of everyone, he keeps the order technically alive by padding its rolls and cadging funds, and takes on Newton Pulsifer as a new recruit.
characters.name: Sergeant Shadwell

characters.description: Shadwell's neighbor, a kindly middle-aged woman who works as a part-time medium and offers other discreet services. Warm-hearted and unbothered by Shadwell's grumbling, she takes an interest in the sour old witchfinder living down the hall.
characters.name: Madame Tracy

characters.description: A seventeenth-century English witch and prophetess whose book, The Nice and Accurate Prophecies of Agnes Nutter, Witch, is the only wholly correct book of predictions ever written. Long dead before the main events, she foresaw the future with uncanny, often maddeningly cryptic precision, and her descendants have puzzled over her prophecies ever since.
characters.name: Agnes Nutter

recaps.ending: Armageddon is averted not by Heaven or Hell but by the free will of a single ordinary child. As the End Times arrive, the Antichrist, Adam Young, comes fully into his powers, but rather than destroying the world he has grown up loving, he refuses the role written for him. Confronted with the machinery of the Apocalypse, Adam dismisses the Four Horsemen, faces down the arriving forces of Heaven and Hell, and rejects Satan himself, denying that the being is truly his father because his real father is the human man who raised him. By choosing humanity over destiny, Adam calls off the end of the world, and reality settles back into place. In the aftermath, Aziraphale and Crowley must answer to their furious superiors for having sided with the world instead of the war. Forewarned by a final prophecy of Agnes Nutter, they swap appearances, so that when Hell tries to execute Crowley and Heaven tries to punish Aziraphale, each survives the ordeal meant for the other, and their masters give up on them. Newton Pulsifer and Anathema Device are left together, having burned the last of Agnes's prophecies to live their own lives free of foreknowledge. Adam returns to being an ordinary boy in Lower Tadfield, and the two old friends from opposite sides sit down to enjoy the world they saved.
recaps.in_short: The angel Aziraphale and the demon Crowley have spent millennia on Earth and, having grown fond of the world and of each other, dread the coming Apocalypse. The Antichrist has been born, but through a mix-up at the hospital the diabolical baby is sent home with an ordinary English family instead of the intended one, and grows up as Adam Young, a normal boy in the sleepy village of Lower Tadfield, while Heaven and Hell fuss over the wrong child. As Adam turns eleven and Armageddon approaches, his latent powers begin to wake, reshaping the world around him according to his boyish whims. Aziraphale and Crowley scramble to prevent the end of the world, aided and hindered by the witch Anathema Device, guided by her ancestor Agnes Nutter's uncannily accurate prophecies, and the hapless witchfinders Newton Pulsifer and Sergeant Shadwell. The Four Horsemen gather and the forces of Heaven and Hell mass for the final battle. In the end, Adam refuses the destiny chosen for him, rejecting his role as Antichrist and using his power to send the Horsemen away and defy his infernal father, stopping Armageddon by human choice. The world is saved, and Aziraphale and Crowley cleverly evade punishment from their respective sides.

recaps.text: The end of the world is scheduled, and neither the angel Aziraphale nor the demon Crowley wants it to happen. After thousands of years stationed on Earth, the two have come to love human life and, quietly, each other's company, and they would rather the world went on. The trouble is that the Antichrist has been born and is meant to be delivered to a prominent family so that he can grow up to trigger the Apocalypse. But a mix-up at the hospital sends the wrong baby home, and the true Antichrist is raised as Adam Young, an ordinary, imaginative boy in the tranquil English village of Lower Tadfield, while Heaven and Hell keep their eyes on the wrong child entirely. As Adam grows toward his eleventh birthday and the appointed day draws near, a sprawling cast is drawn toward Lower Tadfield, including a witch guided by a book of unnervingly accurate old prophecies and a pair of bumbling witch-hunters, all of them caught up, knowingly or not, in the countdown to Armageddon.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, now working alongside the Knight of the Cross Michael Carpenter to deal with a wave of ghosts and spirits that have turned violent. More established than in his first cases but no less broke or reckless, Harry is stalked by an old debt and by his own habit of taking on more than he can safely carry. His fierce loyalty to the people he loves is about to be turned into a weapon against him, and his temper about to cost him more than he imagines.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: A Knight of the Cross, one of a tiny number of mortals chosen to wield a holy sword against the worst evils in the world. Michael carries Amoracchius, a blade said to hold one of the nails of the Crucifixion, and fights with a faith as solid as his broad shoulders. A devout Catholic and a devoted husband and father, he is Harry's opposite in temper - patient, humble, and certain where Harry is cynical and profane - and he becomes Harry's steadfast partner in hunting the tormented spirits plaguing the city. He disapproves of Harry's rough edges but trusts his heart.
characters.name: Michael Carpenter

characters.description: Michael's wife: heavily pregnant, fiercely devoted to her large family, and openly hostile to Harry, whom she blames for drawing her husband into danger. Strong-willed and unafraid to say exactly what she thinks, Charity guards her home and children with everything she has, which makes her and her unborn child a target when Harry's enemies choose to strike at those he cares for.
characters.name: Charity Carpenter

characters.description: Harry's faerie godmother, a Sidhe noblewoman of the Winter Court, beautiful and utterly without human mercy. Long ago Harry bargained away a claim on himself to her, and now the Leanansidhe means to collect - to take him into Faerie and remake him as her own creature. She pursues him through the book, an elegant, patient predator who offers help laced with traps, bound by faerie rules that Harry must exploit to keep his freedom.
characters.name: The Leanansidhe

characters.description: The reporter who chases the supernatural, and Harry's girlfriend, still pressing for the truth of his world and still refusing to be protected from it. Susan's closeness to Harry makes her a mark for the enemies circling him, and her determination to be part of his life draws her toward the vampires' orbit and a danger far greater than any story.
characters.name: Susan Rodriguez

characters.description: The Red Court vampire Harry humiliated during his first case, returned far more powerful and poised. Now elevated among her kind and hosting a grand masquerade ball to mark her rise, Bianca has spent the years plotting a patient, elaborate revenge. Beneath the gracious hostess is a cold, vindictive predator who has arranged events across the city to draw Harry into a trap of her making.
characters.name: Bianca

characters.description: A malevolent spirit tormenting first the ghosts and then the living of Chicago, growing stronger with each victim. It stalks people through their dreams, poisoning and draining them, and singles out those closest to Harry. It proves to be the risen ghost of Kravos, a murderous sorcerer Harry and Michael destroyed not long before; freed and warped in death, and set loose by others for their own ends, it has become one of the deadliest things Harry has faced.
characters.name: The Nightmare

characters.description: A languid, beautiful young man who appears at Bianca's masquerade and, to Harry's surprise, quietly takes his side. Thomas is a vampire of the White Court, whose kind feed on human emotion and desire rather than blood and who wear their humanity far more convincingly than the Red Court. Vain, charming, and hard to read, he has reasons of his own for helping Harry survive the ball, and an interest in him that he does not explain.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: A lovely, fragile young woman who attends the masquerade at Thomas's side, bound to him as his lover and the source he feeds upon. Devoted to Thomas despite what he is, Justine moves through the vampires' world in constant quiet danger, and her bond with him hints that this White Court vampire is not quite as heartless as his kind are meant to be.
characters.name: Justine

characters.description: An ancient and terrifying vampire of the Black Court - the classic bloodsucking undead of legend, rotted and inhumanly strong. Mavra is a sorceress as well as a monster, able to work magic few of her kind command, and she attends Bianca's gathering as a guest of appalling power. Cold, patient, and centuries old, she marks Harry as an enemy worth remembering.
characters.name: Mavra

recaps.ending: Harry destroys the Nightmare - the ghost of the sorcerer Kravos - ending the plague of tormented spirits, and with Michael he saves Charity Carpenter and her newborn son. But the cost of the case is enormous. At Bianca's masquerade, Susan Rodriguez was bitten and infected with the Red Court's curse; caught between human and vampire and terrified of what she might do to the people around her, she leaves Chicago, and Harry, behind. Harry's furious massacre of Bianca and her court, in violation of the guest-truce, has dragged the entire White Council into open war with the Red Court - a war they hold him responsible for starting, and one that will shadow him for years. Thomas Raith, the White Court vampire who unexpectedly helped him, slips away with his secrets and his unexplained interest in Harry intact. Michael Carpenter is now Harry's closest and most trusted ally. Harry ends victorious over the immediate evil but heartbroken, isolated by loss, and freshly burdened with a war he never meant to start and a Council that trusts him even less than before.
recaps.in_short: Working alongside Michael Carpenter, a Knight of the Cross who wields a holy sword, Harry Dresden confronts a wave of ghosts driven violent across Chicago while dodging his faerie godmother, the Leanansidhe, who has come to claim an old debt. The disturbances are the work of the Nightmare, a dream-stalking spirit that proves to be the risen ghost of a sorcerer Harry helped destroy - and it has been set loose deliberately, striking at everyone Harry loves. Behind it all is his old enemy, the Red Court vampire Bianca, now risen in power and staging a grand masquerade as an elaborate revenge. Bianca captures Harry's girlfriend Susan to lure him in; at the ball Susan is bitten and cursed into a half-vampire state, and Harry, enraged, destroys Bianca and her court - an act that ignites open war between the White Council and the Red Court. Harry kills the Nightmare and saves the Carpenters' baby, but Susan, unable to trust herself, leaves him, and he is left blamed for a war.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard and a police consultant, has survived a rogue heart-ripping sorcerer and a tangle of warring werewolves. Along the way he rebuilt his uneasy partnership with Detective Karrin Murphy, gained loyal allies in Billy and the shapeshifting college pack called the Alphas, and stayed under the wary watch of the White Council of wizards. From his first case he carries a dangerous enemy: the Red Court vampire Bianca, whom he humiliated and who has been quietly climbing in power ever since. He is dating Susan Rodriguez, a fearless reporter who chases the supernatural stories he will not give her.

A year on from the werewolf killings, Harry has taken up an unlikely partner: Michael Carpenter, a Knight of the Cross who wields a holy sword against the darkness. Across Chicago the barrier between the living world and the spirit realm has grown thin, and ghosts are rising in torment and turning violent. Harry and Michael hunt these disturbances down one by one, but it becomes clear that something is deliberately stirring the dead into a frenzy. Meanwhile Harry is stalked by his own faerie godmother, the Leanansidhe, who has come to collect an old debt and carry him into Faerie, and he must dodge her elegant traps while the spirit crisis worsens.

The force behind the rising dead reveals itself as the Nightmare, a spirit that hunts people through their dreams, draining and torturing them and growing stronger with every victim. It targets those closest to Harry - striking at Michael's pregnant wife Charity and their unborn child, and at others in his circle - to wound him through the people he loves. Harry realizes the Nightmare is the risen ghost of Kravos, a sorcerer he and Michael had destroyed, and that someone freed and unleashed it on purpose. As he races to protect his friends and unmask whoever is directing the spirit, an engraved invitation arrives: the Red Court vampire Bianca, his old enemy, is hosting a grand masquerade ball.

The threads converge on Bianca. Recovered from the humiliation of their first encounter and risen high among the Red Court, she has orchestrated the whole crisis as an intricate revenge, and her ball is the trap at its heart. She seizes Susan to force Harry to attend. Bound by the customs of such a gathering and desperate to save Susan, Harry and Michael walk into a hall full of monsters: Red Court nobles, the ancient Black Court sorceress Mavra, and other horrors. There Harry gains one unexpected ally in Thomas Raith, a White Court vampire who takes his side for reasons of his own, while the ball tightens around them as a carefully sprung snare.

The masquerade turns to violence. The vampires spring their trap, and Susan is bitten and infected with the Red Court's curse - left half-turned, forced from then on to fight an endless thirst. Enraged past reason, Harry breaks the guest-truce and destroys Bianca and much of her court in a storm of fire, but the act carries a terrible price: it is a declaration of open war between the wizards' White Council and the Red Court, a war the Council will blame on him. With Thomas and Michael's help, Harry and the survivors escape the ruin of the ball.

Harry hunts down and destroys the Nightmare, the ghost of Kravos, ending the torment of the city's dead, and he and Michael save Charity and her newborn son. But the greater damage is done. Susan, now cursed and struggling to keep from fully becoming a vampire, cannot stay near the people she might harm and leaves Chicago and Harry behind. Harry's slaughter at Bianca's ball has dragged the entire White Council into a war with the Red Court that will hang over him for years. He ends the book victorious over the immediate threat but stripped of the woman he loves, blamed for a war, and bound more tightly than ever to Michael Carpenter, who has become his truest ally.
